newsitem.title: UK: Avianca aims for high-yield ex-UK cargo.
newsitem.headline: Avianca aims for high-yield ex-UK cargo.

text.p: Colombian airline Avianca said it will aim at carrying high-yield, mainly low volume cargo traffic on its new twice-weekly London Heathrow-Bogota passenger services, due to start on May 2.

Gil Harding, director of the carrier's UK cargo general sales agent ANA Aviation Services, said this policy would be followed because of the tonnage limitations of the Boeing 767-200s that will be used.
He declined to estimate the payload capability of the plane, which can carry much less cargo than more powerful extended range versions of 767-200/300s .
He would also not comment on the level of rates he planned to charge, apart from saying they would be lower than those quoted by British Airways.

But Harding added that Avianca's rates would be higher than the average 1.20 stg per kg for a 100 kg shipment available from airlines offering ex-London transhipment services to Colombia via Continental Europe.
Other UK-Bogota airfreight connections are available via Miami, often at rates below one stg per kg/100 kg, market sources said.
Harding said ANA hoped to finalise its rate tariff for the route later today.
"There is plenty of trade between Colombia in both directions and I see good airfreight potential for this route," he added.

"From the UK, we expect to be carrying shipments of pharmaceuticals and Scotch whisky as well as general freight. In the reverse direction, flowers will be the main cargo, although I also have a Colombian textile manufacturer interested in booking space," he said. -Bob Murphy, Reuters Air Cargo Service, Tel +44 171 542 7706; fax +5017
